literal: Taizu Yelü Abaoji, Part One
idiomatic: Annals of Taizu Yelü Abaoji, Part One

literal: The Taizu, Great Sage, Great Brightness, Divine Martial, Heavenly Emperor — surname Yelü, taboo name Yi, courtesy name Abaoji, childhood name Chuilizhi — was a native of Yelü Mili village, Xiasiyishi Lie, Dieci Department of the Khitan.
idiomatic: Taizu, styled the Great Sage and Bright Divine Martial Heavenly Emperor, bore the surname Yelü; his given name was Yi, his courtesy name Abaoji, and his childhood name Chuilizhi. He came from Yelü Mili in the Xiasiyishi Lie of the Khitan Dieci branch.

literal: <1> He was the eldest son of Emperor Dezu; his mother was Empress Xuanjian, née Xiao.
idiomatic: <1> He was the eldest son of Emperor Dezu, born to Empress Xuanjian of the Xiao clan.

literal: He was born in the thirteenth year of the Tang Xiantong reign.
idiomatic: He was born in the thirteenth year of Emperor Yizong's Xiantong era (872).

literal: At the beginning, his mother dreamed that the sun fell into her bosom, and she conceived.
idiomatic: Before his birth, his mother dreamed that the sun dropped into her breast, and afterward she became pregnant.

literal: When he was born, the room had divine light and strange fragrance; his body was like that of a three-year-old child, and he could crawl at once.
idiomatic: At his birth, divine light filled the room and a strange fragrance hung in the air. His body was already like a three-year-old's, and he could crawl immediately.

literal: His grandmother, Empress Jianxian, regarded him as extraordinary and reared him as her own son.
idiomatic: His grandmother Empress Jianxian took him for a prodigy and raised him as if he were her own child.

literal: She often hid him in a separate tent, smeared his face, and did not allow others to see him.
idiomatic: She kept him hidden in a separate tent, darkened his face with ash, and forbade anyone else to look upon him.

literal: At three months he could walk;
idiomatic: By three months he could walk;

literal: and he could speak, and knew things before they happened.
idiomatic: and soon he could speak and foretell events yet to come.

literal: He claimed that on his left and right there seemed to be divine beings guarding him with wings.
idiomatic: He said that divine guardians seemed to hover at his sides, winged and vigilant.

literal: Although he was still in childhood, his words always touched upon affairs of state.
idiomatic: Even as a child with baby teeth, he spoke always of public affairs.

literal: At that time his uncle held power over the state; whenever in doubt he would consult him.
idiomatic: His uncle then governed the Khitan, and whenever uncertain he sought the boy's counsel.

literal: When he had grown up, he stood nine chi tall, broad above and tapering below; his gaze pierced people, and he could draw a bow of three hundred jin.
idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he stood nine chi in height — broad-shouldered above, lean below — with a gaze that struck men like an arrow and strength enough to draw a three-hundred-jin bow.

literal: He served as tamun shar.
idiomatic: He held the office of tamun shar.

literal: At that time the Lesser Yellow Shiwei did not submit; Taizu subdued them by stratagem.
idiomatic: When the Lesser Yellow Shiwei refused submission, Taizu took them by strategy.

literal: He attacked the Yuewu, Wugu, Liuxi, Bisha, and other tribes, and conquered them.
idiomatic: He marched against Yuewu and the Wugu, Liuxi, and Bisha tribes, among others, and brought them to heel.

literal: The people of the state called him Azhu Shar.
idiomatic: His countrymen gave him the name Azhu Shar.

literal: In the first year of the Tang Tianfu reign, the year xinyou, Hende Khan was enthroned and appointed Taizu yilijin of the native tribe, put in charge of campaigns; he repeatedly defeated the Shiwei, Yujue, and the Xi chieftain Xialage, capturing many prisoners.
idiomatic: In the first year of the Tang Tianfu era (901), the xinyou year, Hende Khan came to power and made Taizu yilijin of his own branch, entrusting him with military command. Taizu in succession broke the Shiwei and Yujue and the Xi leader Xialage, taking vast numbers captive.

literal: In the tenth month of winter, he was appointed yilijin of the Great Dieci Prefecture.
idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, he was given the post of yilijin of the Great Dieci Prefecture.

literal: The following year, in the seventh month of autumn, with four hundred thousand troops he attacked Hedong and the north of Dai; <2> he captured nine commanderies, taking ninety-five thousand captives, and camels, horses, cattle, and sheep beyond numbering.
idiomatic: The next autumn, in the seventh month, he led four hundred thousand men against Hedong and northern Dai, <2> seized nine commanderies, took ninety-five thousand captives, and won camels, horses, cattle, and sheep past all count.

literal: In the ninth month, he walled Longhua Prefecture south of the Huang River and for the first time built Kaijiao Temple.
idiomatic: In the ninth month he fortified Longhua Prefecture on the south bank of the Huang River and founded Kaijiao Temple.

literal: The following spring, he attacked the Jurchen, subjugated them, and captured three hundred households.
idiomatic: The next spring he campaigned against the Jurchen, brought them down, and took three hundred households.

literal: In the ninth month, he again attacked and captured the Huaiyuan Army and other Hedong garrisons.
idiomatic: In the ninth month he renewed the assault on Hedong and took the Huaiyuan garrison and others.

literal: In the tenth month of winter, he led his army in a raid as far as north of Ji and returned with captives and booty.
idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, he pushed his forces in a foray to the north of Ji and returned laden with prisoners and plunder.

literal: Previously Dezu had captured seven thousand Xi households and moved them to Qinghe in Raole; at this time they were established as the Xi Dieci branch and divided into thirteen districts.
idiomatic: Earlier Dezu had taken seven thousand Xi households and resettled them at Qinghe in Raole; now they were organized into the Xi Dieci branch, divided into thirteen counties.

literal: Taizu was then appointed yue and given overall charge of military and state affairs.
idiomatic: Taizu was thereupon made yue, with full authority over army and state.

literal: The following year, the jiazi year, in the third month, the eastern wall of Longhua Prefecture was expanded.
idiomatic: The next year, a jiazi year, in the third month the eastern quarter of Longhua Prefecture was enlarged.

literal: In the ninth month, he campaigned against the Black-Cart Shiwei; Liu Rengong, Military Governor of the Tang Lulong Army, sent tens of thousands of troops and dispatched his adopted son Zhao Ba to resist.
idiomatic: In the ninth month he marched against the Black-Cart Shiwei. Liu Rengong, Tang governor of the Lulong Army, raised tens of thousands of men and sent his adopted son Zhao Ba to meet him.

literal: When Ba reached Wuzhou, Taizu learned of it through spies and hid crack troops below Peach Mountain.
idiomatic: Ba reached Wuzhou; Taizu, warned by his scouts, lay in wait with elite troops beneath Peach Mountain.

literal: He sent a Shiwei man named Moli, who falsely claimed to have been sent by his chieftain, to arrange a meeting with Ba's forces on the plain.
idiomatic: He sent a Shiwei named Moli to pose as an envoy from the chieftain and invite Ba's army to a rendezvous on the open plain.

literal: When they arrived, the hidden troops sprang up on all sides; they captured Ba, annihilated his force, and pressing the victory routed the Shiwei.
idiomatic: When Ba came, ambushers rose on every side. They took Ba prisoner, wiped out his army, and drove on to shatter the Shiwei.

literal: The following year, in the seventh month, he again campaigned against the Black-Cart Shiwei.
idiomatic: The next year, in the seventh month, he returned to punish the Black-Cart Shiwei.

literal: Li Keyong, Military Governor of Hedong under the Tang, sent the interpreter Kang Lingde to request an alliance.
idiomatic: Li Keyong, Tang's Hedong governor, sent his interpreter Kang Lingde to sue for an alliance.

literal: In the tenth month of winter, Taizu with seventy thousand cavalry met Keyong at Yunzhou; when the banquet was well underway, Keyong asked to borrow troops to avenge his defeat by Liu Rengong at Mugua Ravine, and Taizu agreed.
idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, Taizu brought seventy thousand horsemen to meet Keyong at Yunzhou. Over wine Keyong asked for troops to settle the score with Liu Rengong at Mugua Ravine, and Taizu consented.

literal: They exchanged robes and horses and pledged brotherhood.
idiomatic: They exchanged cloaks and mounts and swore themselves brothers.

literal: When they advanced to attack Rengong, they seized several prefectures and moved all the people away with them.
idiomatic: Marching on Rengong, they overran several prefectures and carried off the entire populace.

literal: The following year, in the second month, they again attacked Liu Rengong.
idiomatic: The next year, in the second month, they struck Liu Rengong once more.

literal: On the return, they raided the Xi north of the mountains and defeated them.
idiomatic: On the homeward march they fell upon the mountain-north Xi and broke them.

literal: Zhu Quanzhong of Bianzhou sent men by sea bearing letters, gifts, robes and belts, and precious objects to offer friendship.
idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong of Bianzhou dispatched envoys by sea with letters, tribute gifts, robes, sashes, and curiosities to propose alliance.

literal: In the eleventh month, he sent a detached force to campaign against the Xi and various tribes, and the unsubmitted Jurchen of the northeast; all were defeated and made to submit.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent a subsidiary army against the Xi and allied tribes, and against Jurchen in the northeast still outside his sway; all were crushed and brought to surrender.

literal: In the twelfth month, Hende Khan died; the ministers, obeying his final command, asked that Taizu be enthroned.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Hende Khan died. The ministers, following his dying wish, pressed Taizu to take the throne.

literal: Helu and others urged him to accept.
idiomatic: Helu and others pressed him to ascend.

literal: Taizu declined three times, then acquiesced.
idiomatic: Taizu refused thrice before yielding to them.

literal: In the first year, on gengyin day in the first month of spring, he ordered officials to set up an altar at the Ru'erwang Assembly Mound; <3> he burned sacrificial wood to announce Heaven and took the imperial throne.
idiomatic: In his first year, on the gengyin day of the first spring month, he had officials erect an altar at the Ru'erwang Assembly Mound, <3> offered burnt sacrifices to Heaven, and ascended the throne.

literal: He honored his mother, née Xiao, as Empress Dowager and installed Empress Xiao.
idiomatic: He raised his mother of the Xiao clan to Empress Dowager and crowned an Empress Xiao.

literal: The Northern Chancellor Xiao Xialage and the Southern Chancellor Yelü Oulisi led the ministers in offering the honorific titles Heavenly Emperor and Earth Empress.
idiomatic: Northern Chancellor Xiao Xialage and Southern Chancellor Yelü Oulisi, at the head of the court, presented the elevated titles Heavenly Emperor for him and Earth Empress for her.

literal: On gengzi day, an edict proclaimed that the imperial clan would succeed the nine tents of the Yaolian clan as the tenth tent.
idiomatic: On gengzi day he decreed that the royal house should take its place as a tenth tent, succeeding the nine tents of the Yaolian line.

literal: On wuwu day in the second month, he appointed his younger cousin Dielidi yilijin of the Dieci Prefecture.
idiomatic: On wuwu day of the second month he named his cousin Dielidi yilijin of the Dieci Prefecture.

literal: That month, he campaigned against the Black-Cart Shiwei and brought their eight tribes to submission.
idiomatic: That same month he marched on the Black-Cart Shiwei and received the submission of all eight of their tribes.

literal: On dingwei, the first day of the fourth month of summer, Zhu Quanzhong, Prince of Liang under the Tang, deposed his sovereign and soon killed him; <4> he declared himself emperor, taking the dynastic name Liang, and sent envoys to announce it.
idiomatic: On the dingwei new moon of the fourth summer month, Zhu Quanzhong, Tang's Prince of Liang, deposed his lord and shortly afterward murdered him; <4> he proclaimed himself emperor under the name Liang and sent envoys with the news.

literal: Liu Rengong's son Shouguang imprisoned his father and styled himself Military Governor of Youzhou and the Lulong Army.
idiomatic: Liu Shouguang, son of Liu Rengong, locked up his father and declared himself governor of Youzhou and the Lulong Army.

literal: On yiyou day in the seventh month of autumn, his elder brother Shouqi, Governor of Pingzhou, led several thousand of his followers to surrender, and they were ordered settled at Pinglu City.
idiomatic: On yiyou day in the seventh autumn month his elder brother Shouqi, prefect of Pingzhou, came over with several thousand men and was resettled at Pinglu City.

literal: On yisi day in the tenth month of winter, he campaigned against the Black-Cart Shiwei and defeated them.
idiomatic: On yisi day that winter, in the tenth month, he attacked the Black-Cart Shiwei and broke them.

literal: On guiyou, the first day of the first month of spring in the second year, he received homage in the main hall from officials and envoys of various states.
idiomatic: On the guiyou new moon of the second year's first spring month, he held court in the main hall to receive the obeisance of officials and foreign envoys.

literal: On xinsi day, the office of tiyin was first established to oversee clan affairs, and his imperial brother Salaci was appointed to it.
idiomatic: On xinsi day he created the office of tiyin to govern the clans and appointed his brother Salaci to the post.

literal: Li Keyong of Hedong died; <5> his son Cunxu succeeded him, and envoys were sent to offer condolences.
idiomatic: Li Keyong of Hedong died; <5> his son Li Cunxu took his place, and Taizu sent envoys with condolences.

literal: On guiyou day in the fifth month of summer, an edict ordered Salaci to campaign against the Wuhuan and Black-Cart Shiwei.
idiomatic: On guiyou day of the fifth summer month he commanded Salaci against the Wuhuan and the Black-Cart Shiwei.

literal: On renzi day in the eighth month of autumn, Youzhou presented a hehuan melon.
idiomatic: On renzi day in the eighth autumn month, Youzhou sent tribute of a twin-fused melon.

literal: On jihai, the first day of the tenth month of winter, the Bright King Tower was built.
idiomatic: On the jihai new moon of the tenth winter month, he erected the Bright King Tower.

literal: A long wall was built at the eastern sea mouth of Zhen.
idiomatic: He constructed a long wall at Zhendong's seaward mouth.

literal: Light troops were dispatched to capture Tuyuhun rebels who had fled into Shiwei territory.
idiomatic: He sent light cavalry to seize Tuyuhun rebels who had crossed into Shiwei lands.

literal: In the first month of spring in the third year, he visited Liaodong.
idiomatic: In the third year's first spring month he toured Liaodong.

literal: On dingyou, the first day of the second month, Liang sent Lang Gongyuan on a diplomatic mission.
idiomatic: On the dingyou new moon of the second month, Liang dispatched Lang Gongyuan as envoy.

literal: In the third month, Liu Shouwen, Military Governor of Cangzhou, was attacked by his brother Shouguang and sent men to request troops to campaign against him.
idiomatic: In the third month Liu Shouwen, governor of Cangzhou, came under attack from his brother Shouguang and sent asking for troops to strike back.

literal: He ordered his imperial brother Sheli Su and the yilijin Xiao Dilu to lead troops to join Shouwen at Beinao Mouth.
idiomatic: He commanded his brother Sheli Su and the yilijin Xiao Dilu to march and rendezvous with Shouwen at Beinao Mouth.

literal: Advancing to the marshland near the Henghai Army, they broke the enemy at the first assault and Shouguang fled in rout.
idiomatic: Pushing to the flats near the Henghai garrison, they shattered the foe at a single drumbeat and Shouguang broke and ran.

literal: Because of this, Beinao Mouth was renamed Alliance Mouth.
idiomatic: Beinao Mouth was therefore renamed Alliance Mouth.

literal: On yimao day in the fourth month of summer, an edict ordered Left Vice Director Han Zhigu to erect a stele at the Daguan Temple of Longhua Prefecture to record meritorious deeds.
idiomatic: On yimao day of the fourth summer month he ordered Vice Premier Han Zhigu to raise a stele at Longhua Prefecture's Daguan Temple commemorating his achievements.

literal: On jiashen day in the fifth month, a sheep market was established north of Coal Mountain to facilitate trade.
idiomatic: On jiashen day in the fifth month he founded a sheep market north of Coal Mountain for commerce.

literal: On jisi day in the tenth month of winter, the Hawk Army was sent to campaign against the Black-Cart Shiwei and defeated them.
idiomatic: On jisi day that winter, in the tenth month, he sent the Hawk Army against the Black-Cart Shiwei and broke them.

literal: The Nianggai tribe of the northwest presented ox-cart drivers as tribute.
idiomatic: The Nianggai tribe from the northwest offered cart-drivers in tribute.

literal: On wuzi, the first day of the seventh month of autumn in the fourth year, his empress's elder brother Xiao Dilu was appointed Northern Chancellor.
idiomatic: On the wuzi new moon of the fourth year's seventh autumn month he named the Empress's elder brother Xiao Dilu Northern Chancellor.

literal: From this time the empress's clan began to hold the chancellorship.
idiomatic: Thus began the custom of appointing the Empress's kin as chancellor.

literal: In the tenth month of winter, the Xi chieftains Kuge, Chaladi, and Chubode of Wumashan rebelled and were suppressed.
idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, the Wumashan Xi leaders Kuge, Chaladi, and Chubode rose in rebellion and were put down.

literal: On bingxu, the first day of the first month of spring in the fifth year, there was a solar eclipse.
idiomatic: On the bingxu new moon of the fifth year's first spring month the sun was eclipsed.

literal: On bingshen day, the Emperor personally campaigned against the western Xi.
idiomatic: On bingshen day the Emperor took the field in person against the western Xi.

literal: The Xi held difficult terrain; their submission and rebellion were inconstant, and repeated summons and persuasion went unheeded.
idiomatic: The Xi barricaded themselves in rugged country, wavering between rebellion and submission; repeated appeals brought no answer.

literal: In this campaign wherever he went he prevailed; he then divided his forces to campaign against the eastern Xi and pacified them as well.
idiomatic: In that campaign he took every stronghold he met; he then split his army to subdue the eastern Xi and pacified them too.

literal: Thus he came to possess all the lands of the Xi and Shiwei.
idiomatic: He now held the full territory of the Xi and Shiwei.

literal: It reached the sea on the east, touched Baitan on the south, Songmo on the west, and the Huang River on the north; all five divisions were entered on the registers.
idiomatic: Eastward it ran to the sea, south to Baitan, west to Songmo, north to the Huang River — five divisions in all, every one entered on the tax rolls.

literal: In the third month, he halted at the Luan River and carved stone to record his achievements.
idiomatic: In the third month he encamped on the Luan River and cut stone inscriptions to commemorate his victories.

literal: He again raided the territory of Jizhou.
idiomatic: He again carried out a raid into Jizhou.

literal: On renshen day in the fourth month of summer, envoys were sent to Liang.
idiomatic: On renshen day of the fourth summer month he dispatched envoys to Liang.

literal: In the fifth month, his imperial brothers Cige, Dieci, Yindishi, and Anduan plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: In the fifth month his brothers Cige, Dieci, Yindishi, and Anduan conspired to rebel.

literal: Anduan's wife Nianmugu learned of it, reported it, and the plot was verified.
idiomatic: Anduan's wife Nianmugu discovered the plot, informed the court, and the charge was proved true.

literal: The Emperor could not bear to execute them; he therefore climbed a mountain with his brothers, sacrificed animals, announced Heaven and Earth as witnesses to an oath, and pardoned their crime.
idiomatic: Unable to bring himself to punish them, he climbed a mountain with his brothers, offered sacrifice, swore before Heaven and Earth, and granted them pardon.

literal: Cige was sent out as yilijin of the Dieci branch, and Nianmugu was enfeoffed as Lady of Jin.
idiomatic: He posted Cige as yilijin of the Dieci branch and ennobled Nianmugu as Lady of Jin.

literal: On renwu, the first day of the seventh month of autumn, Xielidi and envoys of various tribes came to offer tribute.
idiomatic: On the renwu new moon of the seventh autumn month, Xielidi and tribal envoys arrived with tribute.

literal: On jiazi day in the eighth month, Liu Shouguang usurped title at Youzhou and styled himself Yan.
idiomatic: On jiazi day in the eighth month Liu Shouguang seized the imperial style at Youzhou and proclaimed the state of Yan.

literal: On wuwu day in the tenth month of winter, an iron foundry was established.
idiomatic: On wuwu day that winter, in the tenth month, he established an iron foundry.

literal: On renwu day in the eleventh month, envoys were sent to Liang.
idiomatic: On renwu day in the eleventh month he again sent envoys to Liang.

literal: In the first month of spring in the sixth year, Huage was appointed tiyin.
idiomatic: In the sixth year's first spring month he made Huage tiyin.

literal: On wuwu day in the second month, he personally campaigned against Liu Shouguang.
idiomatic: On wuwu day of the second month he took the field in person against Liu Shouguang.

literal: In the third month, he returned from Youzhou.
idiomatic: In the third month he came back from Youzhou.

literal: In the fourth month of summer, You, Prince of Ying of Liang, killed his father and declared himself ruler.
idiomatic: In the fourth summer month Zhu Yougui, Liang's Prince of Ying, murdered his father and seized the throne.

literal: On bingwu day in the seventh month of autumn, he personally campaigned against Shibugu, made them submit, and took captives and booty numbering in the tens of thousands.
idiomatic: On bingwu day in the seventh autumn month he marched in person against Shibugu, received their surrender, and took prisoners and spoil by the tens of thousands.

literal: He ordered his brother Cige to divide forces and attack Pingzhou.
idiomatic: He commanded his brother Cige to split off troops and strike Pingzhou.

literal: On renchen day in the eighth month, the Emperor halted at Mount Ende.
idiomatic: On renchen day in the eighth month he encamped on Mount Ende.

literal: The Prince Li Hu was born.
idiomatic: The prince Li Hu was born.
